nodes.title: Add Silence to Compensate for No OG Video Audio

widgets_values:
{"text":"1. Turn Seamless Video Continuation & Single Pass ON in the Options.
2. Load your video in the Video 1 slot and click the yellow Scissors icon.
  - the left side (beginning) is where your video will start after being stitched together.
  - the right side (end) is where your gen will continue from.
   (IDEALLY your video is 24 FPS and already the correct size/aspect ratio
   as mismatched video can result in imperfect continuations! Use Crop tool to resize.)
3. Select Overlap Frames (5, 22, 39, or 56). This is the # of frames Minimax
     has access to as reference for how to continue your video.
4. If your video has no audio, turn on the OG Vid Has No Audio option to the right.
5. Since this is Single Pass, change your video genning settings:
   - Steps: 6-10+
   - Increase megapixels (since there will be no upscaling, higher is better).
   - Turn off Previews #2 and #3
   - Turn off Final Upscale Pass
6. Prompt! Remember that the first X Overlap frames of your gen are SPOKEN FOR!
   In order to get seamless continuation, start with
   "a single continuous shot from beginning to end" and then describe what's happening
   in a way that the model will understand how it can continue the shot.

Seamless Video Continuation is for changing existing videos, and for creating
single-take shots longer than 15s. It is not a replacement for video editing, and if you 
can get away with cuts then just use normal genning practices with references to your 
previous shots/scenes.\n\nThe more overlap frames, the slower the gen (go figure).","fontSize":14,"fontFamily":"Arial","fontColor":"#000000","textAlign":"left","backgroundColor":"#ffd166","padding":10,"borderRadius":6,"opacity":1,"fontWeight":"normal","lineHeight":1}

nodes.title: Load Audio (15-45 sec is sweet spot)
Length (must be accurate to prevent babbling)

widgets_values:
{"text":"Using the Audio Voice Cloner:
1. Switch it on / Make sure Previews 1-3 are on / Turn Final Upscale Pass off.
2. By default, it uses whatever's loaded in the "Custom Voice Reference" Audio Loader.
   Toggle "Use Custom Voice Reference" OFF to use whatever is loaded into <Audio 1> in the main Ref Loader. 
   If no audio is loaded in <Audio 1> and "Use Custom Voice Reference" is off, the voice will be fully AI generated.
   You can describe the qualities of their voice in the "Tone" text field.
3. Write your line of dialogue.
4. Chose your Tone, the format should be "her tone is..." and proceed from there.
  This is generally where you'd write any line delivery details, inflections, specifics. Can be blank if neutral.
5. Set audio gen length -- Too high and the character babbles to fill the time, too low and they speedrun the line.
  You have to estimate how long it takes to say the line of dialogue at the pace you want.
6. Gen! The files all get saved to output/seedhunter_audio/

------
Useful tips:
- Use *asterisks* to emphasize words in dialogue: "I like *YOUR* muffins, not *HIS*."
- Change your quality to the HIGHest setting if you need to squeeze more emotional width out of the character.
- 16 steps/simple is the best preset I could find so far to balance quality vs. speed.
- Tonal delivery can have a lot of information in it, such as how a character says specific words. Experiment!
- You can tweak the template prompt to fine tune even further.","fontSize":14,"fontFamily":"Arial","fontColor":"#ffffff","textAlign":"left","backgroundColor":"#543a69","padding":10,"borderRadius":6,"opacity":1,"fontWeight":"normal","lineHeight":1}
